records.context: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` uses a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created on the GUI thread. That gives it GUI thread affinity. A queued ``quit()`` goes to the *GUI* event queue rather than the worker queue. The GUI thread immediately enters ``thread.wait()`` during the "drain before closing" behavior in ``ConsolePanel.shutdown``. This blocks the event that would stop the worker and waits for the full timeout even though the worker has finished. ``QThread::quit`` is thread-safe, so the worker thread may call it directly.
records.label: spacr.qt.ai.worker.make_stream_thread#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` is a **DirectConnection**. The QThread object is created here, on the GUI thread, so it is GUI-affine — a queued ``quit()`` is posted to the *GUI* thread's event queue, not to the worker's. Measured: with a queued connection, a GUI thread that goes straight into ``thread.wait()`` (which is exactly what ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` and every "drain before closing" path does) waits out its whole timeout on a worker that has already finished, because the event that would stop the thread is sitting behind the wait. ``QThread::quit`` is explicitly thread-safe, so calling it inline from the worker thread is correct.
records.translation: ``worker.finished -> thread.quit`` er **DirectConnection**. QThread-hluturinn er búinn til hér, á GUI-þræðinum, og er því bundinn GUI — biðraðað ``quit()`` er sett í atburðaröð *GUI*-þráðarins, ekki vinnuþráðarins. Mælt: með biðraðaðri tengingu bíður GUI-þráður sem fer beint í ``thread.wait()`` (sem er nákvæmlega það sem ``ConsolePanel.shutdown`` og hver einasta "drain before closing" leið gerir) allan biðtíma sinn eftir vinnsluhluta sem hefur þegar lokið, vegna þess að atburðurinn sem myndi stöðva þráðinn situr fyrir aftan biðina. ``QThread::quit`` er sérstaklega þráðöruggt, svo það er rétt að kalla á það beint frá vinnuþræðinum.

records.context: These are not a procedural sky of point stars — ``cell.png``'s cyan core fills most of the frame and measures 0.236 in the brightest text-line-sized window, which is far too bright to put white-on-nothing text over. So each master is dimmed at build time by a factor solved from the palette: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returns the brightest a bare window background may be before some role that gets painted straight onto it (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, the status hues) drops below its WCAG minimum, and :func:`solve_dim` scales the image in linear light until the brightest :data:`TEXT_WINDOW`-sized region lands on that number less :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.
records.label: spacr.qt.imagery#13
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: These are not a procedural sky of point stars — ``cell.png``'s cyan core fills most of the frame and measures 0.236 in the brightest text-line-sized window, which is far too bright to put white-on-nothing text over. So each master is dimmed at build time by a factor solved from the palette: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` returns the brightest a bare window background may be before some role that gets painted straight onto it (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, the status hues) drops below its WCAG minimum, and :func:`solve_dim` scales the image in linear light until the brightest :data:`TEXT_WINDOW`-sized region lands on that number less :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.
records.translation: Þetta er ekki reikniritsmyndaður himinn með punktstjörnum — blágrænn kjarni ``cell.png`` fyllir mestan hluta rammans og mælist 0.236 í bjartasta glugganum á stærð við textalínu, sem er allt of bjart til að setja hvítan texta beint ofan á. Því er hver frummynd dekkt við smíði um stuðul sem reiknaður er út frá litaspjaldinu: :func:`spacr.qt.theme.max_background_luma` skilar mestu birtu sem ber gluggabakgrunnur má hafa áður en eitthvert hlutverk sem málað er beint á hann (``fg``, ``fg_muted``, ``accent``, ``fg_dim``, stöðulitirnir) fer niður fyrir WCAG-lágmark sitt, og :func:`solve_dim` kvarðar myndina í línulegu ljósi þar til bjartasta svæðið á stærð við :data:`TEXT_WINDOW` lendir á þeirri tölu að frádregnu :data:`SAFETY_MARGIN`.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The same solve runs again in :func:`render`, where it is a no-op on the shipped masters and the whole guarantee for an image the user dropped into ``~/.spacr/themes`` themselves.

records.context: :mod:`spacr.qt.space` now uses the same three functions — :func:`exposure_target`, :func:`brightest_window` and :func:`solve_dim` — on its generated sky, which for a long time was the one wallpaper in the app that had never been measured against the rule the photographs were held to. It cannot call :func:`solve_dim` on the finished frame (that lands the sky on a solid black rectangle; the numbers are in that module's docstring), so it applies the ceiling where the frame actually breaks the rule and then measures the result here.
records.label: spacr.qt.imagery#15
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :mod:`spacr.qt.space` now uses the same three functions — :func:`exposure_target`, :func:`brightest_window` and :func:`solve_dim` — on its generated sky, which for a long time was the one wallpaper in the app that had never been measured against the rule the photographs were held to. It cannot call :func:`solve_dim` on the finished frame (that lands the sky on a solid black rectangle; the numbers are in that module's docstring), so it applies the ceiling where the frame actually breaks the rule and then measures the result here.
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.qt.space` notar nú sömu þrjú föll — :func:`exposure_target`, :func:`brightest_window` og :func:`solve_dim` — á myndaða himininn sinn, sem lengi var eina veggfóðrið í forritinu sem aldrei hafði verið mælt gegn reglunni sem ljósmyndirnar þurftu að uppfylla. Hún getur ekki kallað á :func:`solve_dim` á fullbúna rammann (það lætur himininn lenda á gegnheilum svörtum rétthyrningi; tölurnar eru í skjölunarstreng þeirrar einingar), svo hún beitir þakinu þar sem ramminn brýtur reglunni í raun og mælir síðan niðurstöðuna hér.

records.context: Everything that decides what a pixel ends up being lives in :mod:`spacr.layers`, which knows nothing about Qt. This module is the part that can only exist with a display: a canvas that paints the model's composite, a layer list that reorders it, and the controls that set the properties the model already knows how to honour.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

This module is the part that can only exist with a display: a canvas that paints the model's composite, a layer list that reorders it, and the controls that set the properties the model already knows how to honour.
records.translation: Allt sem ákveður hvað díll verður að lokum er í :mod:`spacr.layers`, sem veit ekkert um Qt. Þessi eining er sá hluti sem getur aðeins verið til með skjá: strigi sem málar samsetta mynd líkansins, lagalisti sem endurraðar henni, og stýringarnar sem stilla eiginleikana sem líkanið kann þegar að virða.

records.source: Why this canvas paints rather than reusing ``_ZoomView``
records.translation: Hvers vegna þessi strigi málar í stað þess að endurnýta ``_ZoomView``

records.context: :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview._ZoomView` is the right answer when the thing being shown is a finished pixmap: it scales what it was given. Here the zoom is a property of the world, not of the picture — zooming in means :meth:`spacr.layers.Canvas.zoomed` and a fresh render at the new resolution, which is how the labels layer stays crisp at 8× and how the orthogonal-view item gets its slice sliders for free. So the canvas owns a :class:`~spacr.layers.Canvas` and paints; the array→pixmap step still goes through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.numpy_to_qpixmap`, and file loading through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_preview_image`, rather than growing a third copy of either.
records.label: spacr.qt.layer_viewer#4

records.source: :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview._ZoomView` is the right answer when the thing being shown is a finished pixmap: it scales what it was given. Here the zoom is a property of the world, not of the picture — zooming in means :meth:`spacr.layers.Canvas.zoomed` and a fresh render at the new resolution, which is how the labels layer stays crisp at 8× and how the orthogonal-view item gets its slice sliders for free. So the canvas owns a :class:`~spacr.layers.Canvas` and paints; the array→pixmap step still goes through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.numpy_to_qpixmap`, and file loading through :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_preview_image`, rather than growing a third copy of either.
records.translation: :class:`spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview._ZoomView` er rétta lausnin þegar það sem sýnt er er fullbúið pixmap: það kvarðar það sem því var gefið. Hér er aðdrátturinn eiginleiki heimsins, ekki myndarinnar — aðdráttur merkir :meth:`spacr.layers.Canvas.zoomed` og nýja myndun í nýju upplausninni, sem er hvernig merkjalagið helst skarpt við 8× og hvernig hornrétta sýnin fær sneiðasleðana sína án aukavinnu. Því á striginn :class:`~spacr.layers.Canvas` og málar; skrefið fylki→pixmap fer enn í gegnum :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.numpy_to_qpixmap`, og hleðsla skráa í gegnum :func:`~spacr.qt.widgets.live_preview.load_preview_image`, í stað þess að búa til þriðja eintak af hvoru tveggja.

records.context: What turns a drag into ONE action. A brush stroke is dozens of :meth:`move` calls and exactly one thing the user did, so undo has to take back the stroke rather than the last few pixels of it; without a release the tool cannot tell where one stroke ends and the next begins. records.source: What turns a drag into ONE action. A brush stroke is dozens of :meth:`move` calls and exactly one thing the user did, so undo has to take back the stroke rather than the last few pixels of it; without a release the tool cannot tell where one stroke ends and the next begins. Inert by default, like the rest of this class, so a tool that only wants clicks is unaffected.
records.translation: Það sem breytir drætti í EINA aðgerð. Penslastroka er tugir :meth:`move` kalla og nákvæmlega eitt sem notandinn gerði, svo afturköllun þarf að taka strokuna til baka frekar en síðustu dílana í henni; án losunar getur verkfærið ekki greint hvar ein stroka endar og sú næsta hefst. Gerir sjálfgefið ekkert, eins og restin af þessum klasa, svo verkfæri sem vill aðeins smelli verður ekki fyrir áhrifum.

records.translation: Svo, nánar tiltekið, og staðfest í ``tests/qt/test_resource_cleanup.py`` með því að lesa þessa frumkóðaskrá:

records.context: **No process is ever killed.** Not by name, not by "python processes using a lot of memory", not spaCR's own children. There is no ``os.kill``, no ``signal``, no ``subprocess``, no ``Process.terminate()``, no ``QThread.terminate()`` anywhere in this module or reachable from it. The Qt layer removed ``QThread.terminate()`` outright; a stubborn independent execution path is *parked* by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, and that is the strongest thing any of this may do.
records.label: spacr.qt.resource_cleanup#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **No process is ever killed.** Not by name, not by "python processes using a lot of memory", not spaCR's own children. There is no ``os.kill``, no ``signal``, no ``subprocess``, no ``Process.terminate()``, no ``QThread.terminate()`` anywhere in this module or reachable from it. The Qt layer removed ``QThread.terminate()`` outright; a stubborn thread is *parked* by :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, and that is the strongest thing any of this may do.
records.translation: **Ekkert ferli er nokkurn tíma drepið.** Ekki eftir nafni, ekki eftir "python processes using a lot of memory" (ferli sem nota mikið minni), ekki einu sinni undirferli spaCR sjálfs. Það er ekkert ``os.kill``, ekkert ``signal``, ekkert ``subprocess``, ekkert ``Process.terminate()``, ekkert ``QThread.terminate()`` neins staðar í þessari einingu eða aðgengilegt frá henni. Qt-lagið fjarlægði ``QThread.terminate()`` alfarið; þrjóskum þræði er *lagt til hliðar* af :func:`spacr.qt.bridge.drain_thread`, og það er það sterkasta sem nokkuð af þessu má gera.

The page cache belongs to the kernel and dropping it would slow down the whole machine, spaCR included — it is not a free win, it is a transfer from everybody to nobody.

records.context: :data:`TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE` exposes the frame so that *empty sky* — not the mean — lands on :data:`TARGET_SKY_LUMA`, deliberately, so that a sun stays blown out instead of dragging the whole frame to black. Taken as a statement about one global exposure that is now flatly incompatible with the limit, and both of the obvious ways to force it are ruined pictures. Re-solving the exposure, or dimming the finished frame with :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.solve_dim`, needs a factor of 0.064-0.108; both take the sky's own 40th percentile from 0.00091 to 0.00000, i.e. every faint star and the whole nebula go to pure black, and the peak pixel falls from 236-252 to 67-90. Measured, rendered and looked at: a dark grey smudge.

records.source: :data:`TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE` exposes the frame so that *empty sky* — not the mean — lands on :data:`TARGET_SKY_LUMA`, deliberately, so that a sun stays blown out instead of dragging the whole frame to black. Taken as a statement about one global exposure that is now flatly incompatible with the limit, and both of the obvious ways to force it are ruined pictures. Re-solving the exposure, or dimming the finished frame with :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.solve_dim`, needs a factor of 0.064-0.108; both take the sky's own 40th percentile from 0.00091 to 0.00000, i.e. every faint star and the whole nebula go to pure black, and the peak pixel falls from 236-252 to 67-90. Measured, rendered and looked at: a dark grey smudge.
records.translation: :data:`TARGET_SKY_PERCENTILE` lýsir rammann þannig að *tómur himinn* — ekki meðaltalið — lendi á :data:`TARGET_SKY_LUMA`, vísvitandi, svo sól haldist yfirlýst í stað þess að draga allan rammann niður í svart. Sé þetta tekið sem fullyrðing um eina sameiginlega lýsingu er það nú algjörlega ósamrýmanlegt mörkunum, og báðar augljósu leiðirnar til að þvinga það skila ónýtum myndum. Að reikna lýsinguna aftur, eða dekkja fullbúna rammann með :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.solve_dim`, krefst stuðuls upp á 0.064-0.108; hvort tveggja færir 40th hundraðshlutamark himinsins sjálfs úr 0.00091 í 0.00000, þ.e. hver dauf stjarna og öll stjörnuþokan verða hreint svört, og hæsti díllinn fellur úr 236-252 í 67-90. Mælt, myndað og skoðað: dökkgrá klessa.

records.context: The reconciliation is that the two rules are about different things. The exposure anchor is about a *pixel with nothing in it*; the WCAG limit is about the mean over a **region the size of a line of text** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), which is the point :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` already makes about photographs — every photograph has a white pixel somewhere and it is a bright *patch* that makes a caption unreadable. A 3 px star inside a 202x48 px text window moves that window's mean by a quarter of one per cent; the whole starfield measured on its own comes to 0.0007-0.0067, i.e. 1-11 % of the limit. A 207 px sun disc fills the window completely and cannot.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The reconciliation is that the two rules are about different things. The exposure anchor is about a *pixel with nothing in it*; the WCAG limit is about the mean over a **region the size of a line of text** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), which is the point :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` already makes about photographs — every photograph has a white pixel somewhere and it is a bright *patch* that makes a caption unreadable. A 3 px star inside a 202x48 px text window moves that window's mean by a quarter of one per cent; the whole starfield measured on its own comes to 0.0007-0.0067, i.e. 1-11 % of the limit. A 207 px sun disc fills the window completely and cannot.
records.translation: Samræmingin felst í því að reglurnar tvær fjalla um ólíka hluti. Lýsingarakkerið fjallar um *díl sem ekkert er í*; WCAG-mörkin fjalla um meðaltal yfir **svæði á stærð við textalínu** (:data:`spacr.qt.imagery.TEXT_WINDOW`), sem er sami punktur og :mod:`spacr.qt.imagery` heldur þegar fram um ljósmyndir — hver ljósmynd hefur hvítan díl einhvers staðar og það er bjartur *blettur* sem gerir myndatexta ólæsilegan. 3 px stjarna inni í 202x48 px textaglugga hreyfir meðaltal gluggans um fjórðung úr einu prósenti; allt stjörnusviðið mælt eitt og sér gefur 0.0007-0.0067, þ.e. 1-11 % af mörkunum. 207 px sólskífa fyllir gluggann alveg og getur það ekki.

records.context: So the exposure anchor is kept exactly as it was — the sky background is unchanged, to the byte — and the limit is enforced where it is actually violated, by compressing the highlights of the **smooth** layers only (:func:`_compress_highlights`, applied to nebula + galaxy + sun + bloom, never to the starfield). The sun therefore does get noticeably darker, which is the accepted cost; the galaxy is barely touched because it was never the offender; the stars keep white cores and diffraction spikes. :func:`_enforce_legibility` then measures the finished frame with the same :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` used on the photographs and applies whatever residual dim is left, so the guarantee is a measurement and not an argument.
records.label: spacr.qt.space#17
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: So the exposure anchor is kept exactly as it was — the sky background is unchanged, to the byte — and the limit is enforced where it is actually violated, by compressing the highlights of the **smooth** layers only (:func:`_compress_highlights`, applied to nebula + galaxy + sun + bloom, never to the starfield). The sun therefore does get noticeably darker, which is the accepted cost; the galaxy is barely touched because it was never the offender; the stars keep white cores and diffraction spikes. :func:`_enforce_legibility` then measures the finished frame with the same :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` used on the photographs and applies whatever residual dim is left, so the guarantee is a measurement and not an argument.
records.translation: Því er lýsingarakkerinu haldið nákvæmlega eins og það var — himinbakgrunnurinn er óbreyttur, upp á bæti — og mörkunum er framfylgt þar sem þau eru í raun brotin, með því að þjappa björtustu svæðum **mjúku** laganna eingöngu (:func:`_compress_highlights`, beitt á stjörnuþoku + vetrarbraut + sól + ljóma, aldrei á stjörnusviðið). Sólin verður því greinilega dekkri, sem er kostnaðurinn sem er samþykktur; vetrarbrautin er varla snert því hún var aldrei sökudólgurinn; stjörnurnar halda hvítum kjörnum og ljósbrotsgeislum. :func:`_enforce_legibility` mælir síðan fullbúna rammann með sama :func:`spacr.qt.imagery.brightest_window` og er notað á ljósmyndirnar og beitir þeirri dekkingu sem eftir er, svo tryggingin er mæling en ekki rökfærsla.

records.source: :func:`exposure_target` is a *linear-light* relative luminance of the finished image. ``_tone_map``'s output is written straight to 8-bit without a gamma encode, so it is an **sRGB signal value**, and the two are a transfer function apart — the 0.0586 limit is a mid-dark grey around ``#444444``, not a 6 % signal. Encode first, then invert ``1 - exp(-x·E)``.
records.translation: :func:`exposure_target` er hlutfallsleg birta fullbúnu myndarinnar í *línulegu ljósi*. Úttak ``_tone_map`` er skrifað beint í 8-bit án gammakóðunar, svo það er **sRGB-merkisgildi**, og á milli þeirra tveggja er yfirfærslufall — 0.0586 mörkin eru miðlungsdökkt grátt í kringum ``#444444``, ekki 6 % merki. records.source: Some behaviour is kept because other code reads it. Categories still collapse — the list is longer than a short screen. Rows still carry ``navKey`` and headers are still ``SidebarSection``, because the theme, the tutorial script and the maturity tests all reach the dock through those names. And :meth:`refresh_visibility` still applies the Alpha/Beta maturity filter and hides a heading whose modules are all filtered out, which is a separate reason for a row to be absent from its section being shut.
records.translation: Sumri hegðun er haldið vegna þess að annar kóði les hana. Flokkar falla enn saman — listinn er lengri en lágur skjár. Og :meth:`refresh_visibility` beitir enn Alpha/Beta-þroskasíunni og felur fyrirsögn þar sem allar einingar hafa verið síaðar út, sem er önnur ástæða fyrir því að lína vanti en að hluti hennar sé lokaður.

records.source: Rank per-object measurements by class-separation performance.

records.context: The default statistic is the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), computed from the Mann–Whitney U statistic. Results are reported as the unit-free separation ``|2·AUC − 1|`` in ``[0, 1]`` together with the direction of the class difference. AUC is rank based and therefore invariant under monotonic transformations; it does not require normality, equal variance or symmetry. These properties allow measurements with different units and distributions to be compared in one ranking.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The default statistic is the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), computed from the Mann–Whitney U statistic. Results are reported as the unit-free separation ``|2·AUC − 1|`` in ``[0, 1]`` together with the direction of the class difference. AUC is rank based and therefore invariant under monotonic transformations; it does not require normality, equal variance or symmetry. These properties allow measurements with different units and distributions to be compared in one ranking.
records.translation: Sjálfgefna tölfræðin er flatarmálið undir ROC-ferlinum (receiver operating characteristic) (AUC), reiknað út frá Mann–Whitney U tölfræðinni. Niðurstöður eru gefnar sem einingalausa aðgreiningin ``|2·AUC − 1|`` á ``[0, 1]`` ásamt stefnu mismunarins milli flokka. AUC byggir á röðum og er því óbreytanlegt undir einhalla vörpunum; það krefst hvorki normaldreifingar, jafnrar dreifni né samhverfu. Þessir eiginleikar gera kleift að bera saman mælingar með ólíkar einingar og dreifingar í einni röðun.

records.context: AUC represents the probability that a randomly selected object from one class has a higher value than a randomly selected object from the other class. It detects stochastic ordering but can miss distribution-shape differences. For example, classes with the same centre but different spread can have an AUC of 0.5 despite differing distributions. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) statistic is therefore computed for every feature. A high KS statistic combined with AUC near 0.5 sets :attr:`FeatureScore.is_shape_not_shift`.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.feature_rank#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: AUC represents the probability that a randomly selected object from one class has a higher value than a randomly selected object from the other class. It detects stochastic ordering but can miss distribution-shape differences. For example, classes with the same centre but different spread can have an AUC of 0.5 despite differing distributions. The Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) statistic is therefore computed for every feature. A high KS statistic combined with AUC near 0.5 sets :attr:`FeatureScore.is_shape_not_shift`.
records.translation: AUC táknar líkurnar á því að hlutur sem valinn er af handahófi úr einum flokki hafi hærra gildi en hlutur sem valinn er af handahófi úr hinum flokknum. Það greinir slembiröðun (stochastic ordering) en getur misst af mun á lögun dreifinga. Til dæmis geta flokkar með sömu miðju en ólíka dreifni haft AUC upp á 0.5 þótt dreifingarnar séu ólíkar. Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) tölfræðin er því reiknuð fyrir hvert einkenni. Há KS-tölfræði ásamt AUC nálægt 0.5 stillir :attr:`FeatureScore.is_shape_not_shift`.

Hvert skref er varið -- C++-helmingurinn gæti þegar verið horfinn þegar Qt hóf eyðinguna.

records.source: Returns True once the PNG — the raster the GUI actually displays — is on disk. A failed *sibling PDF* does not turn that into False, and the asymmetry is deliberate rather than sloppy: the callers turn False into "no pixmap, no thumbnail", so reporting a missing export that way would delete the figure from the gallery over a file nothing has asked for yet. It is logged at WARNING instead, and :meth:`FigureQueue._request_pdf_refinement` notices the absent page, says so, and stops waiting for a render that will never arrive.
records.translation: Skilar True um leið og PNG — rastinn sem GUI birtir í raun — er kominn á disk. Misheppnuð *systur-PDF* breytir því ekki í False, og ósamhverfan er vísvitandi en ekki hroðvirkni: kallendurnir túlka False sem "no pixmap, no thumbnail" (ekkert pixmap, engin smámynd), svo að tilkynna vantandi útflutning þannig myndi eyða myndinni úr myndasafninu vegna skráar sem enginn hefur enn beðið um. Það er í staðinn skráð á WARNING-stigi, og :meth:`FigureQueue._request_pdf_refinement` tekur eftir að síðuna vantar, segir frá því og hættir að bíða eftir myndun sem aldrei mun berast.

records.source: This fallback supports figures without a ``_spacr_replot`` payload by reading plotted values from bars, scatter collections, and data lines on a single axes. Artist-derived data are exact for bar heights and point coordinates but are necessarily lossy for summary artists such as box or violin plots, which do not retain their source observations. Figures created by :func:`spacr.plot.create_grouped_plot` use their attached source frame instead of this fallback.
records.translation: Þessi varaleið styður myndir án ``_spacr_replot`` gagna með því að lesa teiknuð gildi úr súlum, dreifipunktasöfnum og gagnalínum á einu ásakerfi. Gögn sem leidd eru af teiknihlutum eru nákvæm fyrir súluhæðir og punktahnit en tapa óhjákvæmilega upplýsingum fyrir samantektarhluti á borð við kassarit eða fiðlurit, sem halda ekki upprunalegum athugunum sínum. Myndir sem búnar eru til með :func:`spacr.plot.create_grouped_plot` nota áfasta upprunatöflu sína í stað þessarar varaleiðar.

So :func:`compute` is given the loaded frame and the aggregates (:data:`AGGREGATE_FUNCTIONS`) reduce over all of it. Filtering happens afterwards, to the computed column like any other.

records.context: and that line hands anyone who can type into the box — or anyone who can put a saved chart spec in front of the user — the whole interpreter. A spaCR settings file, a shared ``.spacr`` project, a macro pasted from a colleague: all of them would become executable. So the expression is **tokenised, parsed into an AST of six node types, and walked**. There is no ``eval``, no ``exec``, no ``compile`` and no attribute access anywhere in the grammar; a hostile string does not fail a blacklist, it fails to *parse*.

records.context: Why the scores plot is a GraphCanvas

records.source: Why the scores plot is a GraphCanvas
records.translation: Hvers vegna skorritið er GraphCanvas

records.context: A PCA scores plot is a scatter of two continuous columns that a user wants to colour by ``gene``, facet by ``plateID``, and brush to pull a cluster into Annotate. That is the Graph Builder, exactly, with the two columns computed rather than measured. So :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` appends ``PC1…PCk`` to the source frame and :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` is a :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` subclass that draws arrows on top.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pca_view#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A PCA scores plot is a scatter of two continuous columns that a user wants to colour by ``gene``, facet by ``plateID``, and brush to pull a cluster into Annotate. That is the Graph Builder, exactly, with the two columns computed rather than measured. So :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` appends ``PC1…PCk`` to the source frame and :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` is a :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` subclass that draws arrows on top.
records.translation: PCA-skorrit er dreifirit tveggja samfelldra dálka sem notandi vill lita eftir ``gene``, skipta í undirmyndir eftir ``plateID`` og pensla til að draga klasa inn í Annotate. Það er nákvæmlega Graph Builder, þar sem dálkarnir tveir eru reiknaðir frekar en mældir. Því bætir :meth:`PCAResult.scores_frame <spacr.qt.widgets.pca_model.PCAResult.scores_frame>` ``PC1…PCk`` við upprunatöfluna og :class:`PCAScoresCanvas` er undirklasi af :class:`~spacr.qt.widgets.graph_builder.GraphCanvas` sem teiknar örvar ofan á.

records.context: Rows and columns are the **cartesian product** of their structured-data names' levels, empty combinations included, exactly as :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` draws empty panels: a table read by position needs its positions to line up, and one that closes up its gaps tells the reader "there is no row H" when the truth is "row H was measured and is empty". Above :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` the product is abandoned for the observed combinations only, and :attr:`PivotResult.notice` says so — an unreadable table is not more honest than a smaller one that admits what it left out.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.pivot_spec#10
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Rows and columns are the **cartesian product** of their keys' levels, empty combinations included, exactly as :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` draws empty panels: a table read by position needs its positions to line up, and one that closes up its gaps tells the reader "there is no row H" when the truth is "row H was measured and is empty". Above :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` the product is abandoned for the observed combinations only, and :attr:`PivotResult.notice` says so — an unreadable table is not more honest than a smaller one that admits what it left out.
records.translation: Línur og dálkar eru **kartesískt margfeldi** gilda lykla sinna, tómar samsetningar meðtaldar, nákvæmlega eins og :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.graph_spec.facet_grid` teiknar tóma glugga: tafla sem lesin er eftir staðsetningu þarf að staðsetningarnar standist á, og tafla sem lokar bilunum segir lesandanum "there is no row H" (engin röð H er til) þegar sannleikurinn er "row H was measured and is empty" (röð H var mæld og er tóm). Yfir :data:`MAX_ROWS` × :data:`MAX_COLS` er margfeldinu sleppt og aðeins athugaðar samsetningar notaðar, og :attr:`PivotResult.notice` segir það — ólæsileg tafla er ekki heiðarlegri en minni tafla sem viðurkennir hverju hún sleppti.

records.context: Every cell of a :class:`PivotResult` carries its **n**, whether or not the user ticked it, and the panel prints it. A mean over four objects and a mean over four thousand are the same three digits on application view, and the difference between them is the difference between a result and a coincidence. records.source: Every cell of a :class:`PivotResult` carries its **n**, whether or not the user ticked it, and the panel prints it. A mean over four objects and a mean over four thousand are the same three digits on screen, and the difference between them is the difference between a result and a coincidence. Making n opt-in would make the most important number on the table the one nobody turns on.
records.translation: Hver reitur :class:`PivotResult` ber sitt **n**, hvort sem notandinn hakaði við það eða ekki, og glugginn prentar það. Meðaltal yfir fjóra hluti og meðaltal yfir fjögur þúsund eru sömu þrír tölustafirnir á skjánum, og munurinn á þeim er munurinn á niðurstöðu og tilviljun. Ef n væri valkvætt yrði mikilvægasta talan í töflunni sú sem enginn kveikir á.

records.context: A cell for a combination that has **no rows at all** is empty in every layer, including n. ``0`` is a count of something, and a grid where "no objects were measured in D7" looks identical to "some were measured and none survived the filter" is a grid nobody can read. :attr:`PivotResult.present` keeps the two apart, and :meth:`PivotResult.is_empty` is what the renderer asks.

records.source: A cell for a combination that has **no rows at all** is empty in every layer, including n. ``0`` is a count of something, and a grid where "no objects were measured in D7" looks identical to "some were measured and none survived the filter" is a grid nobody can read. :attr:`PivotResult.present` keeps the two apart, and :meth:`PivotResult.is_empty` is what the renderer asks.
records.translation: Reitur fyrir samsetningu sem hefur **alls engar línur** er tómur í hverju lagi, þar á meðal n. ``0`` er fjöldi einhvers, og net þar sem "no objects were measured in D7" (engir hlutir voru mældir í D7) lítur eins út og "some were measured and none survived the filter" (sumir voru mældir en enginn stóðst síuna) er net sem enginn getur lesið. :attr:`PivotResult.present` heldur þessu tvennu aðskildu, og :meth:`PivotResult.is_empty` er það sem myndarinn spyr um.

records.context: **Cancel** and **Stop** are also different words. A live view's Cancel throws the pass away: nothing it produced is kept, because a half -segmented field is not a result. A hyperparameter search's Stop (:class:`spacr.qt.screens.hyperparam.HyperparamPanel`) finishes the trial in flight and keeps every trial already scored, marking the result partial. Same button position, deliberately different verbs, because a user who presses one expecting the other loses either nothing or hours.

records.translation: **Cancel** og **Stop** eru líka ólík orð. Cancel í virkri sýn fleygir yfirferðinni: engu sem hún framleiddi er haldið, því hálf -sundurgreint sjónsvið er ekki niðurstaða. Passing the user's choice there therefore segmented with ``cpsam`` whatever they picked, including a checkpoint they had just trained in spaCR's own Train Cellpose module. :func:`spacr.utils._resolve_cellpose_pretrained` is what the pipeline uses: it maps the legacy pre-SAM names onto ``cpsam`` and says so once, and returns a path unchanged when the name is a fine-tuned checkpoint.
records.translation: ``model_type=`` er tekið við og hunsað af Cellpose 4 — það skráir "not used in v4.0.1+" og sleppir því, og skilur ``pretrained_model`` eftir á sjálfgefnu ``cpsam``.
